name: Herzeloyde

attributes.attribute: Arthurian heroine and princess of Wales who demanded a truly heroic husband
offered her hand to the winner of a tournament, claimed by the warrior Gahmuret
moved to a small woodland cottage after Gahmuret's death and raised her son Percival there

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Herzeloyde is an Arthurian heroine. She was a princess of Wales. She refused to marry just anyone. She demanded a man who was truly heroic. She announced that the winner of a tournament would win her hand as well. After years of adventure in the east, the warrior Gahmuret arrived in time to claim the prize. Gahmuret was footloose. After he impregnated his bride he left for the east again. There his luck ran out and he was slain. Heartbroken, Herzeloyde moved to a small woodland cottage. There she gave birth to her son, Percival. She intended to keep him from all knowledge of his heritage. His heroic blood found its way out. When Percival was old enough he joined King Arthur at Camelot.
objective: Document Herzeloyde, the Arthurian heroine and mother of Percival.
key_results: Record her refusal to marry anyone but a truly heroic man.
Describe her union with the warrior Gahmuret and his death in the east.
Note her son Percival's rise to join King Arthur at Camelot.
